artisan.summary: Grew up sweeping a craft workshop, then apprenticed there, picking up a trade, an eye for detail and a knack for calming fussy customers.

charlatan.summary: A tavern-circuit con artist who sold gullible marks fake potions, forged papers and other comforting lies.

entertainer.summary: Raised among travelling fairs and carnivals, trading odd jobs for lessons from performers, and still hungry for an audience.

farmer.summary: Worked the fields and herds for years, gaining patience, a sturdy constitution and respect for the weather and wilds.

guard.summary: Stood long watches on a town wall, scanning outside for raiders and inside for thieves and troublemakers.

guide.summary: Lived rough in the wilderness, leading travellers through it and learning a little nature magic from druids along the way.

hermit.summary: Spent early years in isolation far from any town, with animals for company and plenty of time to ponder life's big questions.

merchant.summary: Trained under a trader or shopkeeper, buying and selling goods and hauling them from market to market.

noble.summary: Born into a minor aristocratic family, given a fine education and a close-up view of courtly power and leadership.

sailor.summary: A seasoned hand at sea who has weathered storms and swapped tales in countless harbour taverns.

scribe.summary: Trained as a copyist in an archive, cloister or office, producing careful, error-free documents by hand.

wayfarer.summary: Grew up homeless on city streets, scraping by on odd jobs and the occasional theft, yet never giving up hope.
